BiblicalUsage: Shaçah is a near twin of the last word, to plunder and strip bare. In the days of the judges the LORD delivered Israel into the hands of spoilers, and Isaiah sees the end of it, a people robbed and spoiled, snared in holes with none to deliver, and the psalmist cries that those who hate them spoil for themselves.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that being spoiled is the just end of a people that spoils God's covenant, and the God who gave the land can give it to spoilers.
